days.title: Western Lakes and Panoramas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Müritz
stops.detail: The Müritz, with an area of 117 square kilometers, is the largest body of water located entirely within Germany.

stops.name: Feisnecksee
stops.detail: Apart from the Müritz, which is only located to a small extent in the national park, larger bodies of water in the western part are the Feisnecksee, Rederangsee, Specker See and Woterfitzsee.

stops.name: Käflingsberg
stops.detail: The highest elevation in the generally flatter Müritz part is the Käflingsberg at 100.3 m above sea level.

stops.name: Käflingsbergturm
stops.detail: Located here is the Käflingsberg Tower, a combined observation, fire watch, and mobile communications tower.

days.title: Eastern Heights and Glacial Remains
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Hirschberg
stops.detail: In the Serrahn sub-area, the Hirschberg (143.7 m above sea level) and the Warsberg (143.2 m above sea level) are the highest elevations in the national park.

stops.name: Serrahner Berge
stops.detail: Other significant elevations are the Serrahner Berge at 124.2 m above sea level.

stops.name: Wienpietschseen
stops.detail: The latter are today scattered throughout the landscape as lakes (for example the Wienpietschseen) and kettle holes.
